title: A Museum That Lets Science Speak

paragraphs.en: The town's science museum used to display objects behind glass. Its new director wanted visitors to discover how ordinary machines work, so she invited a retired engineer to build a workshop. At the entrance, a bronze bicycle stood beside an elastic belt and a pressure gauge. Children could push a pedal and watch a pendulum move. There was no examination to pass. The aim was to make physics less remote by connecting an unfamiliar principle with something visitors had already touched, heard, or ridden. A passage through the workshop became a journey from personal experience into scientific explanation.
paragraphs.zh: 小镇的科学博物馆过去只把展品放在玻璃后面。新馆长希望参观者发现日常机器如何运作，于是邀请一位退休工程师搭建工坊。入口处，一辆青铜色自行车旁放着弹性皮带和压力表。孩子可以踩踏板，观察摆锤运动。这里没有需要通过的考试，而是把陌生原理同大家触摸过、听过或乘坐过的东西联系起来，让物理不再遥远。穿过工坊的通道，也意味着从个人经验走向科学解释。

paragraphs.en: The first experiment concerned thermal energy. Water in a clear cylinder expanded as its temperature rose on a centigrade scale. A valve controlled its flow, while a buffer prevented sudden changes in pressure. Students measured movement to the nearest millimeter and then compared it with a centimeter ruler. One group recorded velocity; another examined how a wedge reduced the force needed to lift a load. Their data did not always agree. Rather than hiding the difference, the engineer asked them to repeat each measurement and discuss which decimal place their equipment could reasonably support.
paragraphs.zh: 第一个实验研究热能。透明圆筒中的水随着摄氏温度升高而膨胀。阀门控制水流，缓冲装置避免压力骤变。学生把移动距离量到毫米，再用厘米刻度尺对照。一组记录速度，另一组研究楔子如何减小举起重物所需的力。数据并不总是一致。工程师没有掩盖差异，而是让大家重复测量，讨论仪器究竟能可靠地支持小数点后哪一位。

paragraphs.en: In the materials room, visitors compared an alloy with a pure metal and learned why sulfur can change a compound's properties. The synthesis of a new material often depends on conditions that cannot be seen directly. An oxide coating, for example, may protect a surface rather than merely spoil its appearance. A model triangle illustrated symmetry, and a moving light represented an electron without pretending to show its actual size. Nearby, a carefully shielded display explained radioactive decay. An x-ray image revealed a hidden crack in a tool, demonstrating why looking at the outside is sometimes insufficient.
paragraphs.zh: 在材料展室，参观者比较合金与纯金属，了解硫为什么能够改变化合物的性质。新材料的合成常常取决于肉眼看不到的条件。例如，氧化物涂层可能保护表面，而不只是破坏外观。三角形模型展示对称性，移动的灯光代表电子，但并不声称展示了电子的真实大小。附近经过严格屏蔽的展品解释放射性衰变。工具的X光照片显示内部裂纹，说明有时只看外表远远不够。

paragraphs.en: The electrical section began with an analogue radio. Its antenna received a signal that a microphone could help reproduce during a simple demonstration. A volt described electrical potential, whereas a watt measured power; confusing them could lead to an unsafe design. An old engine's horsepower rating offered a useful comparison, although the museum stressed that different units describe different things. A quart container from an imported machine prompted a discussion of measurement conventions. The internet made conversions easy, but a search result was no substitute for understanding what was being measured and why the distinction mattered.
paragraphs.zh: 电学展区从一台模拟收音机开始。天线接收信号，在简单演示中，麦克风帮助重现声音。伏特描述电势，瓦特衡量功率；混淆两者可能造成不安全的设计。旧发动机的马力标注提供了有用的比较，不过博物馆强调不同单位描述不同事物。进口机器配套的夸脱容器引出对计量习惯的讨论。互联网让单位换算很方便，但搜索结果无法代替对测量对象及其意义的理解。

paragraphs.en: Up on the roof, a botany project linked technology to living systems. Plants grew in trays whose base contained sensors, and readings showed how roots responded to heat. Volunteers found out that a clever device could still fail if its designer forgot the organism it served. That was what the workshop was about: learning a way to ask better questions. From the bicycle to the garden, each display encouraged visitors to test a claim rather than accept an attractive explanation. Science became more approachable, not because it was simplified beyond recognition, but because people could see how evidence gradually earned their trust.
paragraphs.zh: 屋顶上的植物学项目把技术同生命系统联系起来。种植盘底部装有传感器，读数显示根系如何对热作出反应。志愿者发现，即使装置设计精巧，若忽略了它服务的生物，也仍会失败。这正是工坊的核心：学习怎样提出更好的问题。从自行车到花园，每个展品都鼓励人们检验主张，而不只是接受好听的解释。科学变得容易亲近，不是因为被过度简化，而是因为人们看见证据如何逐步赢得信任。
